wu: Future Timeline: Draw a timeline on the board from 2024 to 2040. Students write one thing they did last year and predict one thing they will do next year using 'I will/won't'.
wuAlt: Prediction Ball: Toss a ball and ask 'Will you...?' questions (e.g., 'Will you eat pizza this week?'). Students respond with 'Yes, I will' or 'No, I won't'.
Flashcard Future: Show flashcards of activities (e.g., 'travel', 'study'). Students make sentences like 'I will travel to Casablanca'.
pres: Show a video clip of Moroccan teens predicting 2040 (e.g., 'We will have flying cars'). Highlight 'will/won't + maybe/probably' on the board. Drill sentences like 'Maybe we will have robots at school'. Check understanding with 'thumbs up/down' for true/false predictions.
presAlt: Future Forecast: Display weather symbols (sun, rain) and use them to model 'It will probably be sunny tomorrow'. Students repeat and swap symbols to practice.
Prediction Cards: Give students cards with prompts (e.g., 'school in 2030'). They write predictions and share, focusing on 'will/won't'.
prac: Agree/Disagree Corners: Label two corners 'Agree' and 'Disagree'. Read a prediction (e.g., 'People won't use phones in 2040'). Students go to the corner and explain why using 'I agree because...' or 'I disagree because...'.
pracAlt: Prediction Chain: Students sit in a circle. Each adds to a prediction chain (e.g., 'I will study English. You will travel. He will...').
Fill-in-the-Blanks: Worksheet with sentences like 'In 2030, I ___ (learn) to drive'. Students complete with 'will/won't'.
ls: Listen to 3 short audio clips of teens predicting their future (e.g., 'I will become a doctor'). Students write 'Likely' or 'Unlikely' next to each prediction on their worksheet.
re: Future Charades: Students act out a future action (e.g., 'flying a drone'). Others guess using 'Will you...?'
prod: Prediction Panel: Groups create a poster with 5 predictions about 2040 (e.g., 'Morocco will host the World Cup'). They present to the class using 'We think... will probably...'.
rw: Read a list of 10 predictions about 2030 (e.g., 'Everyone will have a robot'). Students rank them 1-5 (most likely to least likely) and write 3 sentences about their own predictions.
st: Sing 'What Will the Weather Be?' song with actions. Close with 'Today we learned to make predictions with will/won't. Thank you, class!'
g: Students write 9 predictions in a grid. T reads sentences; they cross off matches and shout 'Bingo!'
T holds up cards with verbs; students race to say 'will' or 'won't' + the verb.
Roll a dice; students make predictions about the number (e.g., 'It will rain 7 times this week').
Pick a card with 'maybe/probably'; use it to complete a sentence like 'Maybe I will visit...'.
Teams line up; each student adds to a prediction and the next team member agrees/disagrees.
diff: Fast finishers: Draw a comic strip of their 3 predictions for 2030.
Support: Use sentence starters like 'I will ___ because ___' to scaffold writing.
hw: Write 3 predictions about your family in 2030 (e.g., 'My brother will get married').
Interview a family member: Ask them to predict 1 thing about you in 5 years and write it down.
Watch a short video about the future; write 1 prediction you agree with and 1 you disagree with.
tip: Use local examples (e.g., 'Oujda will have a new library') to make predictions relevant. Teens engage more when connected to their community.
